memos.argument: A hydrogen sensing PCBA is the sensing core of a gas analysis apparatus; heading 9027 names gas or smoke analysis apparatus, and CROSS (967081, 967082) classes gas detectors with a sensor under 9027.10.20. Chapter 90 note 2(a)/(b) sends a part principally for such an instrument to the instrument's heading, so a dedicated PCBA falls in 9027.90.59.10 (parts of 9027.10.20 articles); if presented as a complete working detector, 9027.10.20.00. N330417 shows a PCB classed in 9027.90.
exclusions_against: Ch90 note 2: parts only follow the instrument if suitable solely or principally for it; a generic PCBA with a sensing element could fall to 9033
Ch85 PCBA/sensor rulings (N325069) went to 8543.70 when board is not dedicated to a particular instrument
Facts missing: whether sensor is electrochemical (analysis) and whether it is a bare PCBA

memos.argument: If the board detects/monitors hydrogen presence as a checking device rather than analyzing gas composition, it is a measuring or checking instrument not elsewhere specified in ch90, 9031.80.80. H154038 classed an item in 9031.80.80.
exclusions_against: Heading 9031 text 'not specified or included elsewhere in this chapter' defers to 9027 for gas analysis apparatus
A bare PCBA is at best a part; ch90 note 2(a) sends parts to the heading of the instrument

memos.argument: As a PCBA with sensing element not tied to a specific instrument, it is a ch90 part or accessory of residual type under note 2(c), 9033.00.90.00.
exclusions_against: Note 2(c) applies only when parts are not principally for a particular instrument; hydrogen-detection function points to 9027 per note 2(b)
Note 2(a) excludes goods themselves in ch85 headings (e.g., 8543) from 9033; 9033 is residual of last resort
